name: What is the best home addition layout for a narrow Los Angeles lot?

mainEntity.name: What addition layout works best when my lot is narrow and I do not want to lose the yard?
mainEntity.text: What addition layout works best when my lot is narrow and I do not want to lose the yard?

acceptedAnswer.text: On a narrow Los Angeles lot, the design should maximize usable square footage without making the yard feel boxed in. Rear additions are often the most practical because they preserve street appearance and can avoid widening the house into side setbacks. Second-story additions are another strong option when the structure can support the extra load and the neighborhood context makes vertical expansion appropriate. Some homes benefit from a partial addition combined with a better interior layout, which can create the feeling of a larger home without a huge footprint increase. The best choice depends on existing lot coverage, privacy from neighboring homes, natural light, and how outdoor space is used. A good plan should also protect circulation so the added space does not create long hallways or awkward room shapes. In dense neighborhoods like North Hollywood, Glendale, and Burbank, the design usually succeeds when the addition improves function while keeping the lot open and balanced.
acceptedAnswer.description: For narrow lots, the best layouts usually extend the home at the rear, add above an existing footprint, or reconfigure interior circulation instead of widening outward. The right option depends on setbacks, sunlight, privacy, and how much yard you want to preserve. Vertical additions often create more space with less lot coverage.
